title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-39
content:
2024-11-20 - Morning runbook / scratchpad

Top priorities:
- [ ] Confirm capacity add for Dedicated cluster before next deploy (target: +8 A100s to gpu-provisioner-03)
- [ ] Finish network MTU troubleshooting for pod-to-pod cross-rack traffic (packet drops at ~9000B observed)
- [ ] Validate updated nvidia-driver + CUDA stack on staging nodes (nodes: stg-gpu-*-pool)

Notes / recent context:
- Customer spike last night; autoscale triggered but queue latencies spiked ~200ms for short requests. Looks like batching backlog + one noisy node (gpu-provisioner-03-n-12). Ticket JIRA-5421 opened.
- Found kernel dmesg messages on n-12: GPU ECC corrected errors but rate higher than baseline — set to monitor. Might be thermal throttling? Node in rack 7 (cold-aisle inverted airflow).
- Mellanox firmware mismatch on two nodes causing link flaps; networking team pushed quick fix but follow-up needed to ensure persisted after reboot.

Quick checklist / commands to run:
- Verify node health (k8s): kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide | grep NotReady
- Check recent pod restarts: kubectl -n redwood-inference logs -l app=inference --since=2h | grep -i error
- NVML diagnostics: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION,ECC | tee /tmp/nvidia-dump-$(date +%F).txt
- Check dmesg on suspect node: ssh ops@gpu-provisioner-03-n-12 sudo journalctl -k -n 200 | tail -n 80
- Check ixgbe/mellanox links: sudo ethtool -S eth0 | egrep "rx_|tx_"

Capacity planning notes:
- Current committed Dedicated pools: 120 A100-equivalent. Expected Q1 demand shows +30 additional A100-eq needed. Proposal: stagger procurement and prioritize regions with highest P95 load (us-west-2, eu-west-1).
- Short-term: reserve +8 A100 nodes in us-west-2 on Dedicated for canary traffic. Coordinate with finance for procurement window (procurement lead: Priya).

Networking follow-ups:
- Work with networking (owner: Luca) to validate MTU across VPC peering tunnels. Suspect jumbo frames not enabled consistently on transit gateways.
- Action: schedule 1hr maintenance window (low traffic) to flip MTU flags and test end-to-end (suggest: 02:00-03:00 UTC Fri).

Driver / software updates:
- Staging upgrade flow: 1) cordon node 2) drain workloads 3) apt update + reinstall nvidia-driver 530.41 4) reboot 5) smoke test with short inference jobs 6) uncordon.
- Smoke test script: scripts/staging/gpu-smoke.sh (run with --repeat 3 --concurrency 4)
- Rollout notes: do 3 nodes at a time, monitor llm latency and OOM events. If >3% error rate, rollback.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want to enable ECC strict alerts at 1 corrected-error/min threshold? currently set to 5/min. (pros/cons: noisy vs early detection)
- Confirm whether noisy-node bench shows thermal sensor drift; ask SRE to run ipmitool sensor list for node n-12.
- Follow-up doc: consolidate MTU settings and testing checklist in Confluence page (linked_artifacts above)

Hand-off notes for on-call (if I get pulled into meetings):
- Priority 1: block new Dedicated capacity allocations if any node in the target pool shows >10% GPU utilization variance across peers for 10m window.
- Priority 2: if network link flaps persist after firmware fix, escalate to networking and mark node cordoned until resolved.

Mini retrospects from last incident:
- What went well: autoscale prevented hard OOMs; canary pool absorbed most traffic.
- What to improve: preflight healthchecks for new nodes (thermal + ECC baseline), better annotation of firmware versions in node labels.

Quick links / useful commands:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/infra/gpu-metrics
- Kibana: https://logs.redwood.ai/app/discover#/?q=cluster:gpu-provisioner-03
- Node SSH: ssh ops@gpu-provisioner-03-n-12

Notes to self:
- Ping Priya about procurement window (email drafted).
- Add runbook step to automatically recreate nv_peer memory on detection of link flaps.
- Clean up stale tickets assigned to me older than 30d (JIRA filter: assignee = Samira AND updated < -30d).

End of scratchpad for now — update after driver rollout and MTU maintenance.
